transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Pulsewave Head of MLOps), Maya (SRE), Carl (Finance), Tara (Product)

Summary: quick QBR-style checkin focused on recent cost spike in August, a 3-hour throughput regression incident on 2026-08-18, ongoing pilot considerations for dedicated capacity, and next-step pilots and security artefacts. Customer asked for clearer unit economics and rollback/failover playbook.

Topics: usage patterns, incident postmortem highlights, cost drivers (batching/kv-cache), Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, security/compliance checklist, roadmap alignment, pilot sizing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: yeah, hey everyone thanks for carving time, um this is our weekly-ish qbr checkpoint for pulsewave, thanks for joining. Jordan you want to kick with your top of mind?
[00:18] Jordan: sure, uh thanks Alex. So overall adoption is up, tokens are up about 2.8x y/y month over month through August, but we saw a couple of big spikes, one on 8/18 that, uh, caused higher latency and some tail errors where our app timed out. We ran the postmort, we captured logs and the incident looks like an interplay between autoscaler thresholds and a specific long-sequence workload.
[00:40] Priya: okay, can you remind us if that traffic was hitting the hosted endpoints or your private deploy?
[00:46] Jordan: hosted, main route was through the Redwood hosted API—sorry there might be older notes calling it Redwooed host, we saw a surge to 4x baseline. Our SLA for the user facing service is 300ms p50, 1.2s p95. During the spike p95 got to 2.6s and several requests hit the 5s client timeout.
[01:10] Maya: and just to add, on our side the issue looked like KV cache misses compounded because of many slightly different prefixes, we have a lot of chat contexts. There was also a small memory pressure on our side that delayed retries.
[01:27] Alex: got it — thanks, that's helpful. Two orthogonal things: immediate mitigation (autoscale config, prefix caching) and longer-term economics (batching, quantization, dedicated capacity). For the incident technical gut check, Priya can share what we saw on the Redwood Console traces and suggest a configuration that reduces tail.
[01:48] Priya: yeah, I'll pull up the traces after this. In general, for chatty prefix-heavy workloads we recommend enabling prefix-KV caching and conservative batch windows — that reduces token work. We also ran a sim with 8-bit quant on a similar model and saw 30% cost drop but with 1-2% token quality delta on the open eval we have.
[02:12] Carl: quick question on the cost number — that 30% is from Dedicated inference or from faster kernels on hosted? How should we compare apples to apples?
[02:21] Alex: good call. So the 30% quant savings was on Dedicated with our quant kernels enabled plus continuous batching. Hosted has similar options but the unit price is different because Hosted includes multi-tenant pricing and infra overhead. For Pulsewave's sustained peak that you mentioned, Dedicated becomes economical above roughly 750k tokens/day steady-state, depending on burst patterns. We'll send a calc.
[02:45] Tara: from product side we need predictability — Finance wants to know committed vs on-demand tradeoffs.
[02:52] Carl: yes, committed is appealing if we can keep the unit within a 10% variance month to month.
[02:59] Priya: note that routing policies can help — keep sensitive traffic on Private or Dedicated, and overflow low-priority tasks to Hosted. Also we can do canary traffic shifts via the Console so you can test rollout with a small percentage.
[03:15] Jordan: security checklist — we need SOC 2 type II, SAML SSO, KMS integration and audit logs preserved for 12 months. Is that standard?
[03:27] Ethan: yep, Pulsewave is in the sweet spot for our Private offering. SOC 2 and SAML are supported, KMS for Private is customer-managed, and audit logs can be exported. We'll attach the compliance pack after the call.
[03:42] Maya: also encryption at rest question — we need FIPS-backed key management for our regulated clients.
[03:48] Alex: good note, for on-prem and VPC we support HSM integrate options, we'll flag that to security.
[03:55] [05:10] Speaker 1 (note: intermittent speaker labeling): can we talk about the August spend blip—what caused it?
[05:18] Priya: looking at the billing, three drivers: 1) higher p95 token usage due to longer conversations, 2) low batching (we saw mostly single-request batches during peak), 3) repeated cold KV cache misses. We also tracked an automated nightly job that accidentally triggered a model retrain fingerprinting routine that hit the API heavily for a window of two hours.
[05:44] Jordan: that job was supposed to run in staging—ops bug. We'll fix. But the larger idea is we need guardrails to avoid surprise jobs spiking production. Any suggestions?
[05:56] Alex: yes, we recommend a rate-limiting token policy on the Redwood side plus quota alerts and a spike detection webhook — we can attach those rules to your account and hook to PagerDuty.
[06:09] Maya: can those quota alerts be at route-level and include token distributions?
[06:14] Priya: yes, Console supports per-route thresholds and token histograms. We'll set up a dashboard snippet for you.
[06:20] Tara: also on roadmap—when can we get faster p95? Our roadmap wants 40% lower latency for critical flows by Q1.
[06:29] Priya: two levers: 1) model distillation to shorter-form models (we can recommend a 2ndary roll), 2) Dedicated plus kernel tuning and batching windows. Distillation affects quality so we should eval with sample prompts.
[06:43] Jordan: what's the expected time to run an A/B eval for distillation vs quant?
[06:47] Priya: typical 2-3 weeks for a small eval set, then another week to look at product metrics. Benchmarking can be parallelized though.
[06:55] Carl: from finance view we need clear unit-econ projection: current cost per 1M tokens, projected with quant/dedicated, and committed tier pricing to decide.
[07:06] Alex: we'll share a committed-capacity spreadsheet with unit economics and a sensitivity analysis for spikes and batch gains.
[07:13] [10:02] Jordan: about the canary: we'd prefer gradual canary with auto-fallback to hosted if error rates climb. Can Redwood support that?
[10:11] Priya: yes, the Smart Routing policy can do percentage cutover and auto-fallback. We can configure health checks and a fallback model variant (smaller model) automatically. We'll show the policy in the Console demo.
[10:26] Maya: what about region failover? We have users in EU and NA—during the 8/18 event our EU region saw disproportionate latency due to routing.
[10:36] Alex: we support region-aware routing; if Dedicated capacity is regional we can route requests to the next region within SLOs. For cross-region failover we can set a replication lag budget.
[10:49] Tara: product asks if we can schedule a 48h "spike rehearsal" test with Redwood to simulate worst-case traffic and verify SLA.
[10:58] Priya: yes we do stress tests, we call them surge rehearsals. We can run a synthetic suite and capture Console traces and cost delta. That helps tune autoscale and batching.
[11:09] Jordan: we'll want to see the rehearse results in a shared spreadsheet, with cost delta per scenario.
[11:15] Alex: agreed — we'll run a baseline and two surge scenarios.
[11:21] [18:00] (longer silence while documents are shared)
[18:03] Priya: I'm uploading an example configs doc to the shared drive: https://redwood.workshare/pulsewave/configs (note: link transcribed, may require AE to re-send).
[18:17] Carl: can you also include committed tier contract terms—minimums, overage calculations, and refund clauses?
[18:25] Alex: yep, we'll include both monthly and annual committed options with an exit/fallback clause for unexpected growth.
[18:33] Jordan: security follow-up — Ethan, can you share SOC 2 Type II report and our SAML integration guide?
[18:39] Ethan: putting that in follow-up pack, plus an HSM integration doc for Private deployments.
[18:44] Maya: regarding audit logs retention, can we get a sample log export format?
[18:48] Priya: yes, sample JSON export will be included.
[18:52] [25:12] Tara: quick P&L thought — if we commit to Dedicated now versus optimize hosted, what's break-even timeframe?
[25:20] Alex: based on your last 30-day average and the projected 2.8x growth, break-even for a medium Dedicated pool is about 3-5 months if you keep batching gains. We'll include a slide with break-even curves.
[25:36] Carl: okay, include sensitivity for a 20% higher burst rate and for lower batch efficiency.
[25:42] Priya: we will. Also note that quantization can be toggled per-model so you can pilot quant for internal-only flows first.
[25:52] Jordan: for the canary, what metrics do we monitor? p50, p95, error rate, token cost, and end-to-end latency.
[25:59] Priya: yes plus KV cache hit ratio and batch size distribution. We'll surface all that in the Console.
[26:07] Alex: let's line up dates: Alex to send pricing and committed options by 2026-09-10; Priya to run 24h dedicated benchmark and post results by 2026-09-14; Jordan to send token histograms by 2026-09-09; schedule canary week of 2026-09-21.
[26:27] Maya: are we including a runbook for failover? We need steps for our on-call to follow.
[26:32] Priya: yes, SRE runbook with rollback play and PagerDuty hooks will be provided.
[26:37] [35:00] Conversation drifts to feature requests and roadmaps: smaller requests logged — better per-route cost attribution, deeper linking from trace to billing line items, and more granular retention controls.
[35:20] Alex: those are good feature asks, will log to product backlog and share short-term workarounds.
[35:28] Jordan: any blockers on our side for starting a pilot?
[35:32] Carl: finance needs the committed pricing sheet and a trial cap so we can approve procurement this month.
[35:40] Alex: we'll prioritize the committed pricing doc.
[35:46] Tara: product wonders if Redwood can provide a test harness with anonymized customer prompts so we can run quality evals without leaking PII.
[35:58] Priya: yes, we have an eval harness and can do redaction steps, we'll coordinate offline.
[36:10] [48:00] Final recap and agreement — Alex reads back next steps and owners.
[48:10] Alex: recap: we'll share pricing and committed tiers, Priya runs benchmark, Pulsewave provides token histograms, we'll schedule surge rehearsal and canary, attach SOC2 and SAML docs, and provide SRE runbook and sample audit log exports.
[48:25] Jordan: that matches our expectations, thanks.
[48:29] Carl: one last ask — can Redwood include an estimate of monthly cost variance under 3 spike scenarios?
[48:36] Alex: yes, sensitivity scenarios will be in the spreadsheet.
[48:40] Ethan: I'll follow up by email with the compliance pack and give point contacts.
[48:45] Jordan: great, thanks everyone.
[48:48] Alex: thanks all, we'll circulate notes and action items.

Meeting end.

Artifacts mentioned: pricing sheet (to be attached), compliance pack (SOC2, SAML guide), pilot benchmark config, surge rehearsal plan, shared drive folder (link above).
